![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14221452/assets/60f01450ff74239f3f9bedcf9dfc4445f9c557bb52584ee79a0ba61b0d8bb6f7.png)

Find the area bounded between the curve defined parametrically as

$$
x=t,\,y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1)
$$

and the $x$-axis for $t\in [0,1].$ Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The unsigned area bounded by the parametric curve 

$$
x=x(t),\,y=y(t),\,{t}_{1}\le t\le {t}_{2}
$$

and the $x$-axis is given by the absolute value of the integral

$$
{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we compute

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain the integral expression

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1)\cdot 1\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1)\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that this integral will give us a positive number since $y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\ge 0$ for all $t\in [0,1].$

Therefore, the area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1)\,\text{d}t \\  & =(t+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1)-(t+1)\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(2\operatorname{ln}⁡2-2)-(1\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡1-1) \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡2-2-(0-1) \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡2-1.\end{aligned}
$$
